title: Baccala Mantecato
subtitle: Venetian whipped salt cod spread
excerpt: Baccala mantecato is a Venetian bar snack -- whipped salt cod beaten with olive oil until it becomes a pale, creamy cloud. It looks nothing like fish when finished. Spread thickly on grilled polenta or toasted bread, it is one of the great Venetian contributions to Italian food.
sourceNotes: A Venetian cicchetti staple, made from stockfish or salt cod that arrived in the lagoon via Nordic trade routes from the fifteenth century onwards. The name means 'beaten' or 'worked' cod.

content.text: Add the oil very slowly, as if making mayonnaise. Too fast and the mixture will not emulsify into a cream.

items.prepNote: use 400g salt cod (baccala) -- soak for 24 hours, changing water 3 times; or use smoked haddock as a substitute

content.text: Place the fish in a saucepan with the milk and garlic. Add enough cold water to just cover. Bring to a gentle simmer.
Poach over a very low heat for 15 minutes until the fish flakes easily. Do not boil.
Lift out the fish and garlic. Discard the skin and any bones. Reserve a little of the poaching liquid.
Put the fish and garlic in a bowl. Beat with a wooden spoon, or use a stand mixer with the paddle attachment.
Add the olive oil in a slow, steady trickle while beating continuously. The mixture should become pale and creamy.
If it seems too stiff, add a tablespoon of the warm poaching liquid and beat again. Season with lemon juice and pepper.
Spoon onto grilled polenta or toast. Scatter over the parsley and serve at room temperature.

items.symptom: The mixture is grainy rather than creamy
items.cause: The oil was added too quickly and the emulsion broke.
items.fix: Start again with a tablespoon of the mix in a clean bowl. Beat vigorously and add the broken mixture in tiny drops, then continue with the remaining oil slowly.

items.cause: The salt cod was not soaked for long enough.
items.fix: Soaking for 24 hours with three water changes is the minimum. If still too salty, serve on unsalted polenta or with plenty of bread to balance it.

items.symptom: The texture is too dense and heavy
items.cause: Not enough poaching liquid was incorporated during beating.
items.fix: Add warm poaching liquid one tablespoon at a time. Beat after each addition. Stop when the texture becomes soft and spreadable.

content.text: Baccala mantecato is found in every bacaro in Venice, served on thin slices of grilled polenta. It is the classic cicchetti alongside a small glass of white wine. The dish connects Venice to its centuries of trade with Norway and Iceland. Outside Venice it is less common, which makes it feel like a city secret.
